propositions.text: The Appellant is a Haitian citizen with four children, three in Haiti and one born in Canada in 2017.
propositions.quote: The Appellant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Haiti. She has four children, three of whom reside in Haiti with their aunt; the youngest child was born in Canada in December 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant is a Haitian citizen with four children, three in Haiti and one born in Canada in 2017.

propositions.text: The Appellant fears returning to Haiti because her brother has harassed, threatened, and been violent towards her over family property, fearing he will kill her.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges she may not return to Haiti because her brother, XXXX (also referred to as XXXX), has harassed, threatened and been violent towards her in the past due to a dispute over family property. The Appellant fears that if she returns to Haiti, her brother will kill her.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges she fears her brother's violence and threats if she returns to Haiti.

propositions.text: The Appellant left Haiti in 2013, lived in Dominican Republic, Brazil for three years, then Mexico in 2016, entered US in 2017, and then Canada in 2017 to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: According to the Appellant's Basis of Claim (BOC), she left Haiti in XXXX of 2013 to go first to the Dominican Republic and then on to Brazil. She spent three years in Brazil. She then moved to Mexico with a common-law partner in XXXX 2016, where she stayed several months. In XXXX 2017, at eight months pregnant, the Appellant entered the United States, while her common-law partner remained in Mexico. She entered Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017 and made a claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant states she left Haiti in 2013, lived in several countries, and entered Canada in 2017 to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant's allegations lacked credibility and rejected her claim.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) determined that the Appellant's allegations lacked credibility and rejected her claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's allegations not credible and rejected her claim.

propositions.text: The Appellant asserts the RPD erred in assessing her credibility.
propositions.quote: The Appellant asserts that the RPD erred in its assessment of her credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred in assessing her credibility.

propositions.text: My role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence and decide if the RPD made the correct decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court states its role is to review all evidence and decide if the RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: I dismiss the appeal; the RPD was correct that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection due to lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal. The RPD's finding that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection was correct. The determinative issue is the lack of credibility of the allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal, agreeing the Appellant lacks credibility and is not a refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: I reviewed the RPD hearing recording, entire record, and Chairperson's Guideline 4 on women refugee claimants.
propositions.quote: I have attentively listened to the recording of the RPD hearing and I have carefully reviewed the entire record. I have also taken into account the Chairperson's Guideline 4: Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

propositions.text: I agree with the RPD that the Appellant's allegations are not credible and the claim should be rejected.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that the Appellant's allegations are not credible and that the claim should be rejected.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to mention her brother wanted to kill her prior to 2008 in her BOC narrative.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's failure to mention that her brother wanted to kill her prior to 2008 in her BOC narrative

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant's allegations lack credibility and notes her failure to mention pre-2008 threats in her BOC.

propositions.text: The Appellant's BOC says she took land from her brother in 2006 and he started harassing her after she built a house in 2008.
propositions.quote: In her narrative, the Appellant wrote that her father died in 1991, leaving to his successors, several pieces of land and some livestock. She recounted that in 2006, when she would have been roughly 25 years old, she took a piece of land from her brother which he did not want to part with but was due to her as part of her inheritance. The Appellant recounts that in 2008, she built a house on the piece of land but this displeased her brother and from that point on ("dÞs ce temps"), he started to harass and threaten her.

propositions.text: At hearing, Appellant said brother wanted to kill her everywhere she went before 2008, contradicting BOC.
propositions.quote: However, at the hearing, when the Appellant was asked whether she had had any problems with her brother prior to 2008, she replied that yes, that everywhere she went he wanted to kill her and did not want her to live in Haiti.

propositions.text: RPD repeated and rephrased question to ensure understanding; Appellant repeated same answer.
propositions.quote: The RPD repeated and rephrased the question to ensure that the Appellant understood, however, the Appellant repeated the same answer.

propositions.text: Appellant could not explain discrepancy between testimony and BOC narrative, only said she wrote it that way.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked her to explain the discrepancy between her testimony and her BOC narrative, the Appellant was unable to provide a reply which answered the question. Instead she simply stated that she wrote it that way in her story, that is the problem she is facing and that is why she left.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's BOC said harassment started in 2008, but at hearing she said threats existed before 2008, and she could not explain this discrepancy.

propositions.text: The Appellant disputes the RPD's finding of an important omission, arguing no new information was added in testimony.
propositions.quote: The Appellant disputes the RPD's finding that this was an 'important omission' from her BOC narrative. The Appellant asserts there was no actual omission because "the appellant did not add any new information in her oral testimony."

propositions.text: The Appellant claims limited ability to reply straightforwardly and that her 'yes' answers were misunderstood.
propositions.quote: In her memorandum, the Appellant also asserts that she has a limited ability to reply to questions in a straightforward manner. It is submitted: "The appellant, at the very outset of the hearing was asked if she objected to the presence of an observer, an interpreter in training, and with a smiling face nodded her head, and said "Yes." She was asked several times if she objected and several times answered "Yes," before she clarified that it was fine for the interpreter in training to observe her hearing. The fact that the appellant answered "Yes" to whether there was any other disputes before this incident, and then reiterated that the dispute with her brother was regarding the land and as set out in her narrative is not an actual omission, much less an important omission that should have led the Member to make a negative inference as to the appellant's credibility."

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred in finding an important omission, citing her limited ability to answer questions straightforwardly.

propositions.text: The Appellant's limited schooling and anxiety likely affected her hearing responses.
propositions.quote: I note the Appellant appears to have only completed 5 years of schooling, and that this might help to explain her manner of speaking during the hearing. I also note the XXXX report on file which states that the Appellant suffers from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. This also suggests that the Appellant was likely anxious during the hearing which could have affected her ability to formulate clear and coherent replies to the RPD's questions.

propositions.text: Counsel conceded the Appellant was a 'difficult historian' likely due to her mental capacity.
propositions.quote: Finally, I note that in her Counsel's final submissions to the RPD, her Counsel conceded that the Appellant was a "difficult historian" and suggested that this was likely due to "her own mental capacity".

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Appellant's limited education, anxiety, and counsel's concession about her mental capacity affecting testimony.

propositions.text: Despite difficulties, testimony should roughly approximate narrative timing and event order.
propositions.quote: While I take all of these factors into account, I note that it would still be reasonable to expect that the Appellant's testimony provide a rough approximation of her narrative in terms of when events happened relative to one another, even if precision in the actual dates is not possible, and in terms of the order in which events occurred.

paragraphs.summary: The court states testimony should roughly match the narrative's timing and event order despite difficulties.

propositions.text: I disagree that the pre-2008 threat discrepancy is a serious omission; likely a careless affirmative answer.
propositions.quote: I therefore disagree with the RPD that the fact that the Appellant testified that her brother was after her even before 2008 signifies that there was a particularly serious omission from her BOC narrative. It seems more likely that she responded in the affirmative to what the RPD had asked without really thinking about it.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees that the pre-2008 threat discrepancy is a serious omission, likely a careless answer.

propositions.text: The Appellant's BOC says she built and lived in a house on her father's land in 2008.
propositions.quote: In the Appellant's BOC narrative, it is written: "En 2008, j'ai fait construire une petite maison sur un des terrains de mon pÞre ou j'habitais avec mes enfants. "

propositions.text: At hearing, Appellant said she never finished building or lived in that house.
propositions.quote: However, at the hearing, the Appellant stated she never finished building the house and never lived in that house.

propositions.text: When confronted, Appellant repeated she never lived there because it was unfinished.
propositions.quote: Again, when confronted with the contradiction, the Appellant was only able to repeat that she had never lived in that house as it was not finished.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found a contradiction between the BOC saying the Appellant lived in a house built in 2008 and her hearing testimony denying living there.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues no contradiction exists; BOC sentence can be interpreted to align with testimony.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that there is no contradiction in this case, as the sentence in her BOC narrative can be interpreted in a way that does not contradict her testimony. The Appellant submits: "ln oral testimony, the appellant made it clear that she was living with her children on her father's land in her mother's house, as she had not completed construction of her house. The BOC narrative sentence, which was a translation to French and English through a Haitian Creole interpreter, bears both interpretations "ln 2008, I built a small house on one of my father's land where I lived with my children" is one possible interpretation. Another, equally valid interpretation of the sentence is "ln 2008, I built a small house on one of my father's land where I lived with my children." The appellant submits that when a sentence can be construed in one of two ways, one which is consistent with the appellant's sworn testimony, and another, which contradicts the appellant's sworn testimony, it is unreasonable, and contrary to the presumption of truth as set out in Maldonado for the Member to insist that there is only one possible interpretation which negates the appellant's credibility."

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the BOC sentence can be interpreted to align with her testimony, so no contradiction exists.

propositions.text: I agree with the Appellant that the contradiction is not clear enough to affect credibility.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Appellant, I do not find that the contradiction to be sufficiently clear to warrant a finding that this diminishes the Appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the contradiction is not clear enough to diminish the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The RPD erred on the pre-2008 omission and house contradiction but these errors are not determinative.
propositions.quote: Though I find that the RPD erred in making this particular finding and in making the finding that the Appellant had omitted to include any reference to mistreatment from her brother prior to 2008, I do not find these errors to be determinative of the appeal.

propositions.text: The RPD correctly noted other problems with testimony sufficient to find allegations not credible.
propositions.quote: This is because the RPD was correct to note, during the hearing, several other problems with her testimony which alone are sufficient to find that her allegations are not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD erred on some findings but other testimony problems justify rejecting the claim.

propositions.text: Appellant testified she left family home in 2008 after brother attacked and moved to Marchand for 6 months before brother found her.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the Appellant testified that after her brother attacked her and burned her house in December 2008, she left the family home in Gonaives to go to the town of Marchand where she rented a house. She stated she stayed there 6 months before her brother found her and began to persecute her by asking neighbours where she was living.

propositions.text: RPD confronted Appellant that BOC says she left family home in 2012 after mother's death and moved to Marchand then.
propositions.quote: The RPD then confronted the Appellant with the fact that according to her narrative she only felt obliged to leave the family home in 2012 after her mother had passed away and it was at that point that she moved to Marchand.

propositions.text: Appellant admitted living in Marchand in 2012 but denied living there before 2012.
propositions.quote: Once confronted with this major contradiction, the Appellant simply stated that, she did live in Marchand in 2012. The RPD then asked her whether she had lived in Marchand before 2012, and the Appellant replied that she had not.

propositions.text: RPD reminded Appellant she said she moved to Marchand in 2008; Appellant said she lived in different houses in Marchand in 2012.
propositions.quote: The RPD reminded her that a few moments earlier she stated that she moved to Marchand in 2008, directly after she was attacked by her brother. The Appellant then replied that she had lived in a different house and moved from one house to another, both of which were in Marchand, in 2012.

propositions.text: RPD asked Counsel to show Appellant Schedule A form showing same Gonaives address from 1996 to 2016.
propositions.quote: Finally, the RPD asked Counsel to show the Appellant her schedule A form on which she had marked the same address in Gonaives from XXXX 1996 to XXXX 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant gave contradictory testimony about when she left family home and lived in Marchand, conflicting with her narrative and Schedule A.

propositions.text: The inconsistent testimony about leaving home after 2008 attack is fatal to credibility.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this confused and inconsistent testimony about what she did after ostensibly being attacked by her brother in 2008, is fatal to the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: Despite limited education and anxiety, it is reasonable to expect knowledge of residence and timing of leaving home.
propositions.quote: Despite the Appellant's limited education and anxiety level, it is reasonable to assume that she would know whether she left her family home directly after being attacked by her brother or some four years later, after her mother's death. It is also reasonable to assume that she would know where she resided in the intervening years between 2008 and when she departed Haiti for Brazil, at least in terms of how many years she spent at one address before moving on to another.

propositions.text: I agree with the RPD that the Appellant's story of persecution by her brother is not believable.
propositions.quote: Consequently, I agree with the RPD that the Appellant's story of being persecuted by her brother is unworthy of belief.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's inconsistent testimony about residence after 2008 attack fatal to credibility and agrees with RPD rejection.

propositions.text: Appellant was interviewed by DHS in US in 2017 with Spanish interpreter; she signed notes as truthful.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was interviewed by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) after entering the United States from Mexico, on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2017. The interview was apparently conducted using the services of a Spanish interpreter. The notes of the interview are on the RPD file. The Appellant signed the interview notes on each page to attest to the truth of her statements.

propositions.text: In DHS interview, Appellant said she feared returning to Haiti due to lack of jobs and desire for better future, no mention of brother.
propositions.quote: The notes reveal that the Appellant explained to the DHS officer that she was afraid to return to Haiti because there are no jobs and because she would like more money and a better future. The DHS notes make no mention of any problem or fears with regards to the Appellant's brother in Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD noted the Appellant's DHS interview omitted any mention of fear of her brother, citing only economic reasons for fearing return to Haiti.

propositions.text: The RPD should not have given any weight to the DHS officer's interview notes due to language and reliability issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the RPD should not have given any weight to the DHS officer's interview notes.

propositions.text: The appellant's native language is Haitian Creole and the US interview is suspect and unreliable for credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The appellant lived in Haiti for the vast majority of her life, and her native tongue is Haitian Creole...the US interview is clearly suspect and cannot reasonably be relied upon to impugn the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The Board should be careful not to place undue reliance on POE statements due to questionable reliability.
propositions.quote: the Board should be careful not to place undue reliance on the POE statements. The circumstances surrounding the taking of those statements is far from ideal and questions about their reliability will often arise.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by relying on DHS interview notes, citing language barriers and reliability concerns.

propositions.text: The RPD did not accept the appellant's explanation of misunderstanding the DHS officer's questions and found much interview information accurate.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not accept the Appellant's explanation that she did not understand the DHS officer's questions...much of the information recorded in the interview notes was accurate

propositions.text: It seems unlikely the appellant selectively misunderstood only questions about reasons for leaving Haiti.
propositions.quote: it seems unlikely that her lack of understanding of the questions was of such a selective nature.

propositions.text: The court does not give weight to the interview notes nor take adverse inference due to language interpretation issues.
propositions.quote: I do not give the interview notes any weight nor do I take any adverse inference from these apparent contradictions, given that the language of interpretation was not one in which the Appellant is proficient.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the interview notes reliable, but the court disagrees and gives them no weight due to language issues.

propositions.text: It was an error for the RPD to give weight to the interview notes.
propositions.quote: Though I feel it was an error for the RPD to have given these notes weight

propositions.text: The error is not determinative of the appeal given other reasons for disbelieving the appellant.
propositions.quote: I do not find it to be determinative of the appeal, given my rationale for disbelieving the Appellant, outlined earlier in this decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in giving weight to interview notes but this error does not decide the appeal.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the appellant's explanation of the CASEC report's use of 'assassiné' as meaning stabbed, not assassinated, because the report was in French.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected this explanation as the letter from the CASEC was written in French, not in Creole, thus it would be reasonable to expect that the French meaning of the word was meant.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the appellant's explanation of the CASEC report's wording due to language differences.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the CASEC report's wording is consistent with her explanation and lack of mention of a corpse.
propositions.quote: the appellant notes that it is consistent with the appellant's explanation of the local use of the word "assasins" that the CASEC report did not make any mention of finding a corpse when they attended at the scene.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the CASEC report supports her explanation of the term 'assasins' and absence of a corpse mention.

propositions.text: The CASEC report does not mention the appellant was alive during investigation or what happened after the attack.
propositions.quote: it also does not mention that the Appellant was still alive when it went to investigate nor what happened to her after the attack.

propositions.text: The report states the council was informed by a third party and neighbors heard the perpetrator say 'He has to terminate her life.'
propositions.quote: The report states that the council was informed of the incident by a XXXX XXXX XXXX and also notes that neighbours heard the perpetrator say: "He has to terminate her life."

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the CASEC report lacks details on the appellant's survival and includes threatening statements heard by neighbors.

propositions.text: The CASEC report should not be given any weight due to apparent errors and inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that given the apparent error and inconsistency in the report, the CASEC report should not be given any weight.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the CASEC report is unreliable and should be given no weight.

propositions.text: The appellant does not contest other RPD findings on supporting documentation inconsistencies and insufficiencies.
propositions.quote: It should also be noted that the Appellant does not contest any of the RPD's other findings with regards to her supporting documentation.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant's supporting documents inconsistent or insufficient to support her allegations due to credibility issues.
propositions.quote: I agree with the RPD that the Appellant's supporting documents are either inconsistent with the Appellant's testimony or are insufficient in and of themselves to support the Appellant's allegations, given the serious issues with the credibility of her testimony.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err regarding the appellant's documentation.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not err with regards to the Appellant's documentation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err in assessing the appellant's inconsistent and insufficient supporting documents.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in assessing the appellant's risk of gender-based persecution by relying on 'resilience' without evidentiary basis.
propositions.quote: the Board looks at the appellant's residual profile as a woman in Haiti and concludes that her "resilience" will protect her from gender based persecution...there is no evidentiary basis

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred in assessing gender-based persecution risk by relying on 'resilience' without evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD considered multiple factors beyond 'resilience' in assessing the appellant's risk of gender-based persecution.
propositions.quote: While the RPD does use the term 'resilience' it is not the only factor which is mentioned as contributing to the Appellant's risk

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD considered multiple factors, not just 'resilience', in assessing gender-based persecution risk.

propositions.text: The appellant did not argue fear of gender-based persecution before the RPD or explain risk in her RAD memorandum.
propositions.quote: the Appellant did not argue a fear of gender-based persecution before the RPD, nor did she explain...why she feels she would be at risk

propositions.text: Even if the RPD erred mentioning 'resilience', the appellant has not shown how this affects her risk allegation.
propositions.quote: Thus, even if the RPD erred in mentioning her 'resilience', the Appellant has not explained how this error would impact an allegation of risk.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the appellant did not argue gender-based persecution risk and has not shown how any RPD error affects her claim.

propositions.text: Objective documentation shows women most vulnerable to gender-based violence in Haiti are displaced, LGBT, young girls, poor, unemployed, or without male protection.
propositions.quote: the objective documentation indicates that the women who are most vulnerable to gender-based violence are those who were displaced since the 2010 earthquake, women from LGBT communities, young girls...those who do not have the protection of a male member of the family.

propositions.text: The appellant does not appear to fall into any vulnerable categories and women head-of-households living alone is common in Haiti.
propositions.quote: The Appellant would not appear to fall into any of these categories. I also note that it is common in Haiti for women to be head-of-households, living alone or with children but without a male partner.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant does not fall into categories most vulnerable to gender-based violence in Haiti.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err in its assessment of the appellant's residual profile.
propositions.quote: I do not find that the RPD erred in its assessment of her residual profile.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD did not err in assessing the appellant's residual profile.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not err in finding the appellant's allegations not credible and no risk of torture, death, or persecution.
propositions.quote: I find the RPD did not err in its finding that the Appellant's allegations are not credible...I am satisfied...that the Appellant would not be personally subjected to a risk of torture, a risk to her life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment...not satisfied the Appellant has demonstrated...serious possibility...persecuted on a Convention ground

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err in credibility and risk findings, dismissing the appellant's claims of persecution.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed and the RPD decision confirmed that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision denying refugee or protection status.
